latest_nl_proof:
Use the standard definition of the Apéry set:
Ap(S,m) = {s in S : s - m not in S}.
Since m = m(S), the element m belongs to S and is the smallest positive element of S.

First consider the case m = 1. Then 1 is in S, and since S is closed under addition and contains 0, every nonnegative integer belongs to S. Hence S = Z_{>=0}. Therefore Ap(S,1) = {0}. There are no integers r with 1 <= r <= m-1, so this is exactly the asserted statement in the case m=1.

Now assume m >= 2. Fix r with 1 <= r <= m-1, and consider
T_r := {s in S : s ≡ r (mod m)}.
We show T_r is nonempty. Because S is a numerical semigroup, Z_{>=0} \ S is finite. Hence there exists N such that every integer n >= N lies in S. Choose t large enough that r + tm >= N. Then r + tm belongs to S and is congruent to r modulo m, so T_r is nonempty.

Since T_r is a nonempty subset of Z_{>=0}, the well-ordering principle implies that T_r has a least element; call it w_r. This least element is unique, because two least elements of a totally ordered set must be equal. Thus for each r with 1 <= r <= m-1 there exists a unique least element w_r of S congruent to r modulo m.

We next prove that Ap(S,m) = {0,w_1,...,w_{m-1}}.

First, 0 belongs to Ap(S,m), because 0 belongs to S and 0-m < 0, whereas S is contained in Z_{>=0}; hence 0-m is not in S.

Now fix r in {1,...,m-1}. We have w_r in S by construction. If w_r - m were in S, then w_r - m would also be congruent to r modulo m and would satisfy w_r - m < w_r, contradicting the minimality of w_r in T_r. Therefore w_r - m is not in S, so w_r belongs to Ap(S,m). Hence
{0,w_1,...,w_{m-1}} is a subset of Ap(S,m).

For the reverse inclusion, let a belong to Ap(S,m). Let r be the residue of a modulo m, chosen with 0 <= r <= m-1.

If r = 0, then a = qm for some integer q >= 0. Since m belongs to S and S is closed under addition, qm belongs to S for every q >= 0. If q >= 1, then a - m = (q-1)m belongs to S, contradicting a in Ap(S,m). Therefore q = 0, so a = 0.

If 1 <= r <= m-1, then a belongs to S and a ≡ r (mod m). By minimality of w_r among elements of S congruent to r modulo m, we have w_r <= a. Since a - w_r is a nonnegative multiple of m, there exists q >= 0 such that a = w_r + qm. If q >= 1, then a - m = w_r + (q-1)m belongs to S, because w_r belongs to S, m belongs to S, and S is closed under addition. This contradicts a in Ap(S,m). Hence q = 0, so a = w_r.

Thus every element of Ap(S,m) is either 0 or one of the w_r, and therefore
Ap(S,m) = {0,w_1,...,w_{m-1}}.

Finally, fix r with 1 <= r <= m-1. Since w_r ≡ r (mod m), there exists an integer k_r such that w_r = r + mk_r. This integer is unique: if r + mk = r + mk', then m(k-k') = 0, so k = k'. It remains to show k_r is positive. Because w_r belongs to S, we have w_r >= 0, so k_r >= 0. If k_r = 0, then w_r = r, which is a positive element of S strictly smaller than m (since 1 <= r <= m-1), contradicting the fact that m = m(S) is the smallest positive element of S. Therefore k_r >= 1.

So for each r with 1 <= r <= m-1, there is a unique positive integer k_r such that w_r = r + mk_r.

This proves the lemma.
role_in_parent: Introduces Apéry representatives and the positive integer coordinates used to encode a numerical semigroup of multiplicity m.
statement_nl: Let S be a numerical semigroup and let m be a positive integer with m = m(S). Then for each residue class r with 1 <= r <= m-1, there exists a unique least element w_r of S congruent to r modulo m, and Ap(S,m) = {0,w_1,...,w_{m-1}}. Moreover each w_r has the form w_r = r + m k_r for a unique positive integer k_r.

domain_restrictions: S is a numerical semigroup (in particular, S ⊆ Z_{≥0}, 0 ∈ S, closed under addition, and cofinite in Z_{≥0})
m is a positive integer satisfying m = m(S) (multiplicity of S, i.e., the smallest positive element of S)
r ranges only over integers with 1 ≤ r ≤ m-1 (nonzero residue classes modulo m excluding 0)
w_r is an element of S and is constrained by the congruence w_r ≡ r (mod m)
k_r is constrained to be a positive integer (k_r ∈ Z_{>0})
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: Fix a numerical semigroup S and let m = m(S). For every integer r with 1 ≤ r ≤ m−1, there exists a unique element w_r ∈ S such that (i) w_r ≡ r (mod m) and (ii) w_r is the least (with respect to the usual order on Z) element of S among those congruent to r modulo m. Then the Apéry set satisfies Ap(S,m) = {0} ∪ {w_r : 1 ≤ r ≤ m−1}. Additionally, for each such r there is a unique positive integer k_r with w_r = r + m k_r.
quantifier_order: ∃! w_r (w_r ∈ S ∧ w_r ≡ r (mod m) ∧ ∀ w ∈ S ((w ≡ r (mod m)) → w_r ≤ w))

variables.domain: subset of Z_{≥0} that is closed under addition, contains 0, and has finite complement in Z_{≥0}
variables.name: S
variables.role: ambient object; determines the semigroup and its Apéry set

variables.name: m
variables.role: multiplicity parameter; assumed to equal m(S)

variables.name: w_r
variables.role: unique least element of S with w_r ≡ r (mod m)

variables.name: k_r
variables.role: unique quotient such that w_r = r + m k_r

witness_dependencies: w_r depends on S and r (and m, since congruence is modulo m)
k_r depends on S and r (and m) through the equation w_r = r + m k_r
